newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy police investigate international child ring.
newsitem.headline: Italy police investigate international child ring.

text.p: Italian police said on Monday they were investigating a possible international child smuggling ring with links to Belgium after a Cambodian man was arrested in Rome airport with a fake passport and four children who were not his.

Cao Leng Huot was arrested on Saturday on arrival at Rome's Fiumicino airport on charges of kidnapping and promoting illegal immigration. He was carrying a stolen Belgian passport, dozens of photographs of other children and telephone numbers in code.

Police said they had arrested a woman on Monday at Fiumicino who was also carrying a Belgian passport apparently stolen at the same time as the one carried by Huot, which police had recognised as being on an international blacklist.
Airport police chief Francesco Girasoli told reporters the case had "international links, which certainly involve Belgium".
Belgian police and Interpol were engaged in the enquiries.
A paedophile and child murder scandal has shaken Belgium for three months.
Huot told police at the airport in fluent French that the two girls and two boys, aged between about six and 12, travelling with him from Phnom Penh via Hong Kong were his children.
But one of the girls shouted out that he was lying and was not their father. The nationality of the children, who have been taken into care, was not clear.
Girasoli said Huot's luggage had contained cash and credit cards as well as around a dozen airline tickets with the names left blank. The children had carried no luggage.

Huot also had a book of around 100 addresses and telephone numbers in Europe. Police said the numbers were written in code and disguised with oriental ideograms. In addition he carried dozens of photographs, mostly of adolescent girls.
